song.title: Symphony No. 5 in C minor, Op. 67 — I. Allegro con brio

source.basedOn: Eulenburg No. 402, ed. Max Unger (1938), IMSLP #575952

notes: Base tempo half note = 104 (quarter = 208): a common modern tempo, close to Beethoven's metronome mark half = 108. Strict tempo everywhere except the fermatas and the bar-268 cadenza (the movement should drive).
Exposition repeat played: bars 1-124 twice (pass 1 and pass 2), then bars 125-502. Bars 123-124 are rests and are kept in tempo before the repeat.

Fermatas are realised in tempoMap: a constant slow tempo over the held part of the bar, then (when cut) a silent caesura in the last 0.05 beat of the bar; notes held under a cut fermata are shortened to end at the cutoff.

Bar 268 cadenza: the tutti chord on the downbeat stays in tempo (one quarter), the oboe G is held (2.4 s from its start, not cut), the cadenza notes F-E♭-D, E♭-D-C-D, F-E♭ play at Adagio quarter = 71 as marked (the edition gives no metronome; 71 is its playback value), the final D is held to about 1.9 s, cut, 0.3 s caesura, then Tempo I.
Bar 268 is shown as conduct = 0 (the conductor shows nothing during the cadenza); every other bar is conducted in one (one beat per bar).
Fermata bar 2: Opening, first fermata (E-flat): held about 2.2 s from the note start; short 0.25 s caesura because the second motto follows at once.
Fermata bar 5: Opening, second fermata (D tied from bar 4): longer than the first, about 3.2 s from the note start; 0.4 s caesura before the p restart of the theme.

Fermata bar 21: Only Violin I holds the G (everyone else plays a quarter-note chord and stops): a short stop inside the flow, about 1.9 s from the downbeat; 0.3 s caesura before the ff motto of bar 22.
Fermata bar 24: Climax of the first paragraph (ff, F tied from bar 23): a little longer than bar 5, about 3.4 s from the note start; 0.4 s caesura before the p restart in bar 25.

Fermata bar 128: Start of the development (strings C#-C#-C#-C, winds hold G from bar 126): about 3.0 s from the strings' C (the winds' G sounds about 3.6 s); a little shorter than the long opening fermata because the development presses on; 0.35 s caesura.
Fermata bar 249: Recapitulation, first fermata: same 2.2 s and 0.25 s caesura as the opening, so the return is heard as the same gesture.
Fermata bar 252: Recapitulation, second fermata: same 3.2 s and 0.4 s caesura as bar 5.

Fermata bar 268 (cadenza G): Oboe cadenza, opening G (the tutti chord is a quarter and stops, the oboes keep the G): held about 2.4 s from the downbeat, not cut, the oboe goes straight on into the Adagio.
Fermata bar 268 (cadenza final D): Oboe cadenza, final D (fermata): the Adagio quarter (about 0.85 s) is held to about 1.9 s, cut, 0.3 s caesura, then Tempo I in bar 269.
Fermata bar 479: Coda, first fermata: same 2.2 s and 0.25 s caesura as the opening.
Fermata bar 482: Coda, second fermata: same 3.2 s and 0.4 s caesura as bar 5.

Dynamics: pp 34, p 48, mp 62, mf 76, f 96, ff 114, fff 124; sf = prevailing level + 12 (max 127) with acc 1; fp = 96 falling to 48 with acc 1 (fp does not occur in this movement). v2 is the level at the note end, v2d (when present) the beats after the onset at which v2 is reached (the level is constant after that; an sf on a long note returns to the prevailing level within half a beat).

cresc./dim. words ramp linearly from the word to the next dynamic marking of the same part (or to the end of the printed dashes when they stop more than one bar earlier); when the next marking goes the other way (Beethoven's cresc. ... subito p, e.g. bars 142-145, 150-153), the ramp rises two steps and the subito marking then drops.
Hairpins follow their printed length and end on the next marking within 12 beats, otherwise one step (bar 268 oboe: f to p over the held G, so the cadenza is p).

Paired winds (one staff in the source edition, two parts in OpenScore): markings that the second part lacks inside its own phrases were taken from its partner: fl2 level 34 bar 233; ob2 level 34 bar 233 cresc. bar 167 dim. bar 268; bn1 level 114 bar 195 level 114 bar 303.

Entries after four or more beats of rest without their own dynamic marking (markings left out in the OpenScore parts, e.g. Violin I has no p after the cadenza in bar 269 and none at the second theme in bars 63 and 307) take the median level of the parts that carry a newer marking at that moment (two or more instruments needed; changed only when two marking steps off, or one step after eight bars of rest): fl1 bar 39 114→96, fl1 bar 91 48→95, fl1 bar 39 (pass 2) 114→96, fl1 bar 91 (pass 2) 48→95, fl1 bar 338 48→76, fl2 bar 43 114→96, fl2 bar 43 (pass 2) 114→96, ob1 bar 36 48→72, ob1 bar 36 (pass 2) 48→72, ob1 bar 217 114→48, ob2 bar 36 114→72, ob2 bar 36 (pass 2) 114→72, ob2 bar 160 114→48, cl1 bar 38 48→96, cl1 bar 38 (pass 2) 48→96, cl1 bar 275 96→67, cl1 bar 325 114→48, cl1 bar 329 114→48, cl1 bar 336 114→67, cl2 bar 38 114→96, cl2 bar 38 (pass 2) 114→96, cl2 bar 213 114→81, cl2 bar 336 114→67, bn1 bar 36 114→72, bn1 bar 36 (pass 2) 114→72, bn2 bar 36 114→72, bn2 bar 36 (pass 2) 114→72, hn1 bar 43 48→96, hn1 bar 43 (pass 2) 48→96, hn1 bar 143 114→62, hn1 bar 342 48→98, hn1 bar 448 96→114, hn2 bar 43 48→96, hn2 bar 43 (pass 2) 48→96, hn2 bar 143 114→62, hn2 bar 342 48→98, hn2 bar 448 96→114, vn1 bar 63 114→48, vn1 bar 63 (pass 2) 114→48, vn1 bar 269 114→48, vn1 bar 307 114→48, vn1 bar 315 114→48, vn1 bar 323 114→48, vn1 bar 327 114→48, vn1 bar 331 114→48, vn2 bar 270 114→48.

The same cresc. in several parts within four beats ends where the others end when a part's own ramp runs more than two beats longer (missing f in the oboes and cellos in bar 19) or its target was only a guess: ob1 18: 48→114 until 22 → →96 until 19; ob1 18': 48→114 until 22' → →96 until 19'; ob2 18: 48→114 until 22 → →96 until 19; ob2 18': 48→114 until 22' → →96 until 19'; hn1 143: 62→96 until 145 → →76 until 145; hn2 143: 62→96 until 145 → →76 until 145; vc 18: 48→114 until 22 → →96 until 19; vc 18': 48→114 until 22' → →96 until 19'.

Articulation: staccato marks give art short; unslurred notes of an eighth or less are short (detached playing at this tempo); slurred notes are sus with a slur group id (the engine joins them legato).

Strings: one-slash tremolo half notes (Beethoven's shorthand for repeated eighths) are kept as one note art trem as the contract asks, with the written subdivision in note.meas (0.5 beat) so the engine can re-articulate them as eighths: bars 45-50, 52-55, 159, 161, 163, 165, 167-169, 172-173, 276-277, 279, 281, 289-294, 375, 377, 379, 381-385, 391-394, 476-477.

Winds and brass: the same one-slash marks are written out as repeated eighth notes (bars 159, 161, 163, 165, 374, 376, 378, 380, 477); a tie into such a bar lengthens the held note by one eighth instead of re-attacking.

Timpani: trill marks and the four-slash note are rolls (one note art roll, bars 249, 251, 346, 354, 479, 481); one-slash half notes are Beethoven's shorthand for repeated eighths and are written out as separate strokes (bars 52-55, 168-169, 172-173, 296-299, 374, 391-394, 423, 425, 427, 429, 431), because a roll would lose the hammering eighths.
Contrabass sounds an octave below the written part (MusicXML octave-change -1). Notes below E1 (played with a C extension): bars 479, 481.

Bowing: a note after a rest of at least one beat starts down-bow; a last-quarter pickup into a downbeat starts up-bow; otherwise strokes alternate; a slur group and a chord are one stroke; ff fermata notes are down-bow. Added standard exceptions: (A) a pickup group after a rest that runs into the next downbeat (the motto: eighth rest, three eighths, long note) starts so that the downbeat is down-bow (U D U | D); (B) pizzicato notes do not count (bow D is written), and the first arco note after pizzicato is down-bow; (C) each tremolo note is one stroke.

Focus (close-up camera) is computed from the notes only, never from the removed annotations: per 2-bar window (cut at fermatas and at the fixed shots), each group's exposed onset energy (onsets weighted by velocity, 0.4 for a repeated pitch, slightly by register, as a share of all groups); tutti when 13+ players of strings, winds and brass play loud. Shots of at least 6 s are chosen by dynamic programming (fit minus 2 s per cut, minus a penalty for shots over 24 s), neighbouring shots differ. Fixed shots (as placed): conductor bars 1-5 (bars 1-5, both passes; 7.2 s); horns bars 51-62 (horn call 59-62; 6.92 s); conductor bars 1-5 (pass 2) (bars 1-5, both passes; 7.2 s); horns bars 51-62 (pass 2) (horn call 59-62; 6.92 s); oboe bars 268-268 (cadenza 268; 10.52 s); tutti bars 463-502 (last 6 bars 497-502; 27.4 s).

Violin II plays the same samples as Violin I; the engine detunes it slightly (see docs/ORCHESTRA_BANKS.md). Player volume/pan are starting values from the seating plan; the final balance is set by the engine from measured bank levels.

Correction vn1-113 (bars 113): Violin I bar 113: the motto upbeat is three repeated notes F5-F5-F5 into G5 (Mutopia; Violin II/Viola/Cello also repeat one note), and the recapitulation parallel bar 365 is D5-D5-D5 in both editions. OpenScore has D5-F5-F5.

Correction winds-114 (bars 113, 114): Woodwinds bar 114: the B-flat of bar 113 is tied over the bar line into the first eighth of 114 (Mutopia), exactly as in the recapitulation parallel bars 365-366 where both editions tie. OpenScore re-attacks an E-flat chord on the downbeat of 114.

Correction bn-151 (bars 151): Bassoons bar 151: eighth rest, E-flat4-E-flat4-D4 (Mutopia), imitating the low strings of bar 150 one bar later, so that bar 152 (C-C-C-B-flat, same in both editions) continues the sequence. OpenScore repeats bar 152 in bar 151 (C4-C4-C4-B-flat3).

Correction cl2-111 (bars 111): Clarinet II bar 111: after the E-flat5 eighth it plays B-flat4 eighths (Mutopia), as Clarinet II does in the parallel bar 115 in OpenScore itself and in the recapitulation parallel bar 362 in both editions. OpenScore has rests.
